# Remove executable-fixture races for #1074

## Summary

Move the existing fake-command dispatcher into `mj-core::test_hooks`, as decided in the issue’s latest comment. Convert all 12 remaining fixture-writing sites in worker and CLI tests so generated scripts are read by interpreters, avoiding the “Text file busy” race.

## Implementation

- Expose `install_fake_command(directory: &Path, program: &str, script: &str)` under `cfg(all(unix, feature = "test-hooks"))`. Preserve its existing behavior: write a `.script` companion and symlink the command name to the checked-in dispatcher.
- Move the executable dispatcher to `mj-core/tests/fixtures/fake-command.sh`, preserve its executable Git mode, and include it in core’s Cargo package allowlist.
- Add a feature-gated `fake_command_dispatcher() -> PathBuf` accessor. Use it both in the installer and in controller move-session tests that currently construct the dispatcher path themselves.
- Enable core’s `test-hooks` feature through dev-dependencies in controller, worker, and CLI. Ordinary test commands must work without extra feature flags; normal builds retain their current defaults.
- Remove the controller-local implementation and update all controller callers to use core directly.
- Convert worker relay fixtures, user-shell fixtures, worker-environment integration fixtures, the harness `executable` helper, and CLI PTY fixtures to the shared installer. Preserve command names, arguments, responses, and existing directory creation.
- For the two Python reviewer fixtures, keep Python source in non-executable files and install separate fake commands whose shell bodies use `exec python3 <quoted-source-path> "$@"`. Use the existing quoting helper. Preserve Python’s stdin, marker locations, PID tracking, and signal behavior.
- Keep production executable provisioning and fixtures already launched through explicit interpreters outside this change.

## Validation

- Add focused core behavior tests covering command lookup with restricted `PATH`, paths and arguments containing spaces, stdout/stderr and exit status, and replacing an installed fake.
- Verify a fake still executes while its `.script` file remains open for writing. Exercise stdin forwarding with more than 64 KiB through the shared subprocess helper.
- Run existing worker reviewer, harness, environment, controller dispatcher-user, and CLI PTY tests with normal parallel execution. Confirm reviewer cancellation and process cleanup remain intact.
- Run `cargo test -p brokk-mj-core --features test-hooks`, the required full `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and formatting checks in the dev profile.
- Check core’s package file list includes the dispatcher, and audit the touched tests for remaining direct execution of scripts written by the multithreaded test process.

## Assumptions and Completion

- Unix fixture behavior and existing Python availability remain unchanged.
- No retries, test serialization, runtime behavior changes, or new crate are needed.
- Commit the validated changes on the current branch; do not push.
I’ll move the dispatcher into core, migrate the fixtures, then run the required tests and commit the fix on the current branch.
